definitions.explanation: Used to express that you want something (a noun). The thing wanted is marked with が.
In the pattern 「～てほしい」, expresses wanting someone else to do something.

examples.notes: Object is marked with が, not を

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{本|ほん}が{欲|ほ}しいです。
{手伝|てつだ}ってほしいんです。
examples.english: I want you to help me.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}のとき、{犬|いぬ}が{欲|ほ}しかったけど、{家|いえ}が{小|ちい}さかったから{飼|か}えなかった。
examples.english: When I was a child, I wanted a dog, but I couldn't have one because my house was small.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{車|くるま}が{欲|ほ}しくなった。
examples.english: I started wanting a new car.
I want you to come quickly.

examples.japanese: {静|しず}かにしてほしいです。
examples.english: I want you to be quiet.

examples.japanese: もっと{努力|どりょく}してほしかった。
examples.english: I wanted you to try harder.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}には{好|す}きなことを{見|み}つけて、{楽|たの}しく{生|い}きてほしいと{思|おも}っています。
examples.english: I want my children to find what they love and live happily.

notes: {欲|ほ}しい conjugates as an i-adjective: {欲|ほ}しくない (negative), {欲|ほ}しくて (te-form), {欲|ほ}しかった (past). Important: Use {欲|ほ}しい for wanting things (nouns), but use ～たい for wanting to do actions (verbs). The pattern ～て{欲|ほ}しい means you want someone else to do something.
